title: Four comforts
hook: whether or not there is another world, a kind and clean heart is safe (AN 3.65)
carry: one kind act, one clean choice

segments.voice: Yesterday: the Kalamas, and your line, check it against what helps. Today, the end of the same talk, the part that's often left out, and the week closes.

After the questions, the Kalamas have agreed that greed, hatred and confusion lead to harm. But one question still hangs in the air, the one the traveling teachers argued about most. What happens after death? Is there another world? Do our deeds bear fruit? Every teacher who came through town had a different answer, and the Kalamas couldn't check any of them. The Buddha doesn't settle the argument. Instead, he describes a person who doesn't need it settled to be at peace.
screen: `THE QUESTION STILL HANGING.` → `WHAT HAPPENS AFTER DEATH?` → `A PEACE THAT DOESN'T NEED THE ANSWER.`

segments.voice: At the end of AN 3.65, the Buddha describes a noble disciple whose heart is free of greed and ill will, unconfused, mindful. Someone who fills the world in every direction with kindness, compassion, gladness for others, and calm. That person, he says, has four comforts here and now. Paraphrased: first, if there is another world, and good and bad deeds bear fruit, then after death I'll arise somewhere good. Second, if there is no other world, and deeds bear no fruit, then here, in this very life, I live free of hostility and trouble, at ease. Third, if evil comes to those who do evil, well, I intend evil toward no one. How could suffering touch me, who do no evil? Fourth, if evil doesn't come to those who do evil, then either way I see myself as clean. Each comfort has an if. Speaking to people who don't yet accept his teaching, the Buddha doesn't ask them to take rebirth or karma on faith. He shows that a kind and clean heart comes out well on every branch. Elsewhere, he teaches rebirth and karma plainly, and Buddhist traditions hold them as central. Here, he meets the Kalamas where they are. The Kalamas, the sutta says, were delighted, and went for refuge. Look back at this week: the fire sermon, read whole, the eye as an ocean, a king hunting the sound inside a lute, the Numbered Sayings, the luminous mind, know for yourselves. And now four comforts, for anyone, whatever they believe.
screen: `A HEART FREE OF GREED AND ILL WILL` · `IF THERE IS ANOTHER WORLD, OR IF NOT` · `IF EVIL RETURNS, OR IF NOT` · `MEETING THE KALAMAS WHERE THEY ARE` · then, large: `FOUR COMFORTS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone you love, and let a simple wish for their well-being warm the chest. Then widen it, to people in this building, this street, this city, in every direction, the way the sutta pictures kindness filling the world, without forcing the feeling. Rest inside that circle, and notice: right now, with a kind heart, nothing needs settling.
Four comforts. In AN 3.65, the one with a kind, clean heart is at ease whether or not there is another world, and whether or not deeds bear fruit. Today's word.
Your line: one kind act, one clean choice. A kind heart comes out well on every branch. That's the week.

howItsDone: Many Buddhists practice the four immeasurables, kindness, compassion, gladness and equanimity, radiating them in every direction, a practice the end of the Kalama Sutta describes.

original.note: Pali assasa: comfort, solace, assurance; the four assasa of AN 3.65.

trapdoor: what you thought: four comforts are four nice feelings.
what it means: in AN 3.65, four assurances for the one with a kind, clean heart: at ease whether or not there is another world, whether or not deeds bear fruit.

what a scholar hears: some modern readers take the four as Buddhist agnosticism, while traditional commentators read them as skillful teaching to newcomers, since rebirth and kamma are affirmed throughout the canon.

chat.says: What if I'm not sure about rebirth or karma? Can Buddhism still help me?
options: Yes: a kind, clean heart is at ease whether or not there's another world.
Only if you pick one of the four comforts first and hold to it.
Only once you've worked out which of the teachers is right.
chat.meaning: In AN 3.65 each comfort has an if: a heart free of greed and ill will comes out well whether or not there's another world.

karma.meaning: action, and the fruit it bears

refuge.meaning: going for refuge: committing to the Buddha's path

noble disciple.meaning: a follower well along the Buddha's path
